title: Repeated Type Code Matching
pattern: Repeatedly branching on a type code or enum variants in multiple methods across the codebase.
why_bad: Violates the Open/Closed Principle. Adding a new type requires searching for and updating every single branch block in the codebase.
detection: Repeated `match` or `switch` statements over the same enum type across multiple functions.
counterexample: Branching on a closed enum that rarely changes (like `Option` or `Result`) or is localized within a single factory function.
fix: Replace type codes with a trait/interface and implement polymorphic methods.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Replace Conditional with Polymorphism"; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 15.2.
